investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, the scheduler cannot place the pod, the VM is never created, and the eval probe times out without producing any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner or application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this observability eval failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever candidates. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is blocked. A recent node label change or taint addition could have reduced the eligible set.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent probe runs (all 3 sibling checks ran within a ~7-minute window and all hit the same constraint).
Lower confidence — node affinity selector in the agent pod spec targets a node group that has been scaled down to zero or cordoned, leaving only the 2 kata-capable nodes which are already saturated.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable slots are available and not fully consumed, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, topology spread) must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing no resources succeeds and the pod schedules normally, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads that have since completed) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the pod spec's affinity rules are confirmed correct, the root cause shifts to a node labeling or taint regression rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner itself threw an exception before submitting the pod (e.g., token expiry, API auth failure), the scheduler message would be misleading and the real failure would be upstream of scheduling — this would be disproved by confirming the pod appears in kubectl get pods with status Pending/Unschedulable.

If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message, a transient race condition on a single probe run would be more plausible; the fact that all three checks independently hit the same constraint makes a transient explanation unlikely.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all cluster nodes and fails with a warning before slots reach 100% utilization, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling is fully blocked.
Add an eval that detects Pending pods older than a configurable threshold in the remote-agents namespace, catching slot leaks from incomplete cleanup before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node-affinity eligibility eval that verifies the expected number of nodes (e.g., at least 2) satisfy the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the minimum.

Consider a sibling-correlation eval rule: when all checks under a feature share the same scheduler error message, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency (infrastructure) failure classification rather than treating each check independently.

No remote agent VM could be provisioned, so the eval runner never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod slots on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every createAgent call in the eval runner times out before a pod is assigned to a node. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment and is confirmed as an eval-layer signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, the scheduler cannot place the pod, the VM is never created, and the eval probe times out without producing any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner or application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this observability eval failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever candidates. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is blocked. A recent node label change or taint addition could have reduced the eligible set.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent probe runs (all 3 sibling checks ran within a ~7-minute window and all hit the same constraint).
Lower confidence — node affinity selector in the agent pod spec targets a node group that has been scaled down to zero or cordoned, leaving only the 2 kata-capable nodes which are already saturated.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable slots are available and not fully consumed, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, topology spread) must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing no resources succeeds and the pod schedules normally, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads that have since completed) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the pod spec's affinity rules are confirmed correct, the root cause shifts to a node labeling or taint regression rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner itself threw an exception before submitting the pod (e.g., token expiry, API auth failure), the scheduler message would be misleading and the real failure would be upstream of scheduling — this would be disproved by confirming the pod appears in kubectl get pods with status Pending/Unschedulable.

If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message, a transient race condition on a single probe run would be more plausible; the fact that all three checks independently hit the same constraint makes a transient explanation unlikely.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all cluster nodes and fails with a warning before slots reach 100% utilization, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling is fully blocked.
Add an eval that detects Pending pods older than a configurable threshold in the remote-agents namespace, catching slot leaks from incomplete cleanup before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node-affinity eligibility eval that verifies the expected number of nodes (e.g., at least 2) satisfy the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the minimum.

Consider a sibling-correlation eval rule: when all checks under a feature share the same scheduler error message, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency (infrastructure) failure classification rather than treating each check independently.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was stuck unschedulable — 2 of 6 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No remote agent VM could be provisioned, so the eval runner never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod slots on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every createAgent call in the eval runner times out before a pod is assigned to a node. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment and is confirmed as an eval-layer signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared VM provisioning path is the common failure point.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is fully consumed, leaving no allocatable slots for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity is misconfigured or the labeled nodes were recently reduced, this would compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — transient cluster saturation: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads (from users or other eval runs) may have temporarily consumed all peer-pod slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion that could self-resolve once existing VMs are released.

LOWER — cluster node count reduction: if the 2 affinity-matching nodes were recently scaled down or cordoned, available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity would drop to zero even if per-node quotas are unchanged.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — VM provisioning (kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduler resource)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks fail with the same Kubernetes Unschedulable message citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity. The VM provisioning layer is the earliest violated boundary (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes node pool — affinity-matching nodes (2 of 6)
affectedAreas.reason: Only 2 of 6 cluster nodes match the pod's node affinity/selector, and both are at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. The other 4 nodes are excluded by affinity, not by resource limits (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch calls createAgent with type 'remote' and blocks on pod scheduling. Because the pod never schedules, no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails for all 5 required fields (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents degraded/outage thresholds
affectedAreas.reason: degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 are configured; with all three checks failing, the feature is at or past the outage threshold in the eval status system (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: check allocatable vs. allocated counts to confirm exhaustion and determine whether capacity needs to be increased or existing VMs need to be released.
Check for leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user sessions that may be holding peer-pod slots without active workloads; terminate any such pods to free capacity.

Review whether the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods is intentional and whether the 2-node pool is the expected size; if nodes were removed or relabeled, restore the pool or update the affinity to match the current topology.
If resource exhaustion is confirmed as sustained rather than transient, evaluate increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes or adding additional affinity-matching nodes to the pool.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in features.json (lines 183-184) and both failed, confirm the feature's eval status reflects degraded or outage state per the degradedAfterFailures=1 / outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent or was a transient saturation event. A pass would produce all 5 required evidence fields; a fail would reproduce the same Unschedulable message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe cluster nodes for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and allocated counts
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the extended resource is exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes and reveals the total capacity ceiling. This is the most direct proof or disproof of the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the affinity-matching nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies what is currently holding the peer-pod slots, whether those are eval artifacts, user workloads, or leaked pods from prior failed runs.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node labels to verify affinity-matching node pool size
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 2-node affinity-matching pool is the expected size or has shrunk due to node removal, cordoning, or label changes, which would reduce total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or quota enforcement issue would need to be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient saturation rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a label that no longer exists on any node), the root cause would shift from resource exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration, and the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would be a secondary symptom on the only nodes that partially matched.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a concurrent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than the shared VM provisioning path.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is registered on any node (i.e., the resource name is unknown to the scheduler), the Insufficient message would appear even with zero demand, pointing to a node plugin or device plugin registration failure instead of capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on affinity-matching nodes and fails with a warning before attempting agent creation, providing earlier and more actionable signal than a scheduling timeout.

Add a cluster-node-affinity-pool eval that asserts the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is at or above a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a kata-peerpods-vm-headroom eval that asserts available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across affinity-matching nodes exceed a minimum buffer (e.g., at least 1 free slot), alerting before full exhaustion.
Introduce a remote-agent-cleanup eval or post-run hook that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval cycle, preventing slot leakage from accumulating across runs.
